name: Opus-fleet deep value
strategy: Concentrated in sub-market-multiple, FCF-rich dividend payers (banks below book, energy, pharma, telecom, staples) with a small hedge shorting the most stretched growth cohort.

positions.thesis: Citigroup trades near 0.7x tangible book and ~9x forward earnings, deeply below intrinsic value; buybacks below book are accretive, CET1 strong, dividend ~3%. Classic deep-value bank re-rating candidate as regional/financials momentum (XLF +6% 1m, KRE +5.5%) confirms sector strength.

Valero at low-single-digit EV/EBITDA and high normalized FCF yield; refining margins supportive, disciplined capex, heavy buybacks plus ~3-4% dividend. XLE +19% 6m signals energy value working. Operationally best-in-class refiner.

Vanguard Value ETF anchors the sleeve in low P/E, low P/B, dividend-paying large caps. Value (IWD +10.7% 3m) is outperforming growth (IWF +5.5%); broad diversified value exposure at 4bps with reliable dividend distribution.
Verizon at ~9x earnings with ~6% dividend yield well covered by FCF; deleveraging, stable cash flows, trades far below intrinsic. Defensive deep-value carry that compounds even in a flat tape.

Pfizer at ~8x forward earnings with ~7% dividend yield near multi-year lows; post-COVID trough pricing ignores durable base pharma FCF and pipeline optionality. Deep-value contrarian with margin of safety on P/E and yield.

Altria at ~10x earnings and ~7% dividend, high FCF conversion and pricing power fund a 55+ year dividend-growth record. Low-beta deep-value cash cow; total-return engine largely independent of market direction.
CVS Health at ~9x earnings and below book on integrated retail-PBM-insurer assets; ~4% dividend, improving MLR guidance. Deep-value turnaround with substantial FCF and margin-of-safety valuation.
General Motors at ~5x earnings, well below book, generating strong auto FCF funding aggressive buybacks that shrink share count. Extreme low-multiple value; capital return offsets cyclical risk.

Semiconductors up +104% 12m and +52% 6m at extreme valuations, the antithesis of deep value; small hedge on the most stretched growth cohort to fund a value-over-growth rotation and cushion drawdowns. Tight stop given momentum.

outlook: Value is quietly outrunning growth (IWD +10.7% vs IWF +5.5% 3m) while mega-cap tech/semis look euphoric (SMH +104% 12m). I want to own the cheapest FCF-generative, dividend-heavy businesses trading below intrinsic value (banks under book, refiners, pharma, telecom, staples) that compound via yield and buybacks regardless of index direction, financed partly by a small short on the most overextended growth. Over a flat-to-choppy H2 tape, the ~5% blended dividend carry plus multiple-normalization offers positive expected return with downside protection from low multiples and stops.
